cells.tense: You are holding several threads and you feel what is fair here without working it out.
cells.ask: Name the call you keep circling, then make it or send it before the day ends, and leave it alone after.
cells.core:
You can tell what is fair without a long argument inside your head. Something surfaces quickly — the sense that an arrangement is right, or that it has drifted — and you act on it. The speed is not carelessness. It is what a clean instrument sounds like.

The same evenness shows in what you give and what you take. You notice when one side has been carrying more than its share and you adjust before anyone says so. What holds this together is not a still point. It is the constant small correction, made without ceremony, that keeps the exchange alive and keeps you in contact with the people in it.
cells.sheetLine: You feel what's fair and move before doubt can argue.
cells.verb: gathering what is true into one line you can act from
cells.place: where you keep steady by adjusting what you add and what you take out

cells.tense: You are already arranging pieces of a conversation that has not happened, rehearsing lines for a meeting that may never come.
cells.ask: Pick the one smallest piece you can finish today, finish only that, and stop without planning the next.
cells.core:
You are reaching for a settled version of this before the ground has settled beneath it. The same active adjustment that keeps things even is running ahead — sensing what to add and subtract from a situation that has not arrived. When it works, that adjustment is easy and right-sized, and you respond to what is actually in front of you. What shows now is the pre-emptive version: planning for outcomes whose first step has not been taken.

What is missing is not strategy. It is the sense that movement can start from something you actually feel, not from what the day is telling you to feel. Acting from the real thing makes the next step simpler. Acting from the imagined outcome adds more to carry.
cells.sheetLine: You're balancing a future that hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You put this down at some point and never picked it up again, and the distance from it is longer than you seem to remember.
cells.ask: Write one true sentence about how you actually feel right now, then read it to yourself once before the day closes.
cells.core:
The gathering is not happening here. Pieces sit where they landed and you have been walking past them. Something you feel is not being let into the room where decisions get made, and the adjustment that should be continuous has gone quiet. What is missing is not a plan. It is the simple contact with what you carry — the kind you get by staying with a feeling long enough to hear it, without asking it to solve anything.

You do not need to fix the whole arrangement. Bringing one piece back into your own hands, on paper you keep for yourself, honors what you feel without handing it to someone else to hold.
cells.sheetLine: You feel it and you've stopped letting it into the room.

cells.tense: You are already keeping things even here, but you describe it as though the balance keeps itself without anyone's hand on it.
cells.ask: Tell one person, once, that you are the one who has been holding this steady, then let the conversation go where it goes.
cells.core:
You are the one adjusting and re-adjusting, sensing when to press and when to wait, and you have been calling that just how things are. The tuning is yours and it runs so constantly it feels like part of the room. When it shows, it looks like a person who is present to what is actually shifting and responds to it directly rather than by rule.

That same instinct connects you to the people involved — the shared sense of what matters, the small marks of recognition that keep the thing alive between you. You have been treating that as background. It is the work. Writing down one moment you re-balanced, and why, gives the doing a place to land. Naming it out loud will not make it fragile.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one holding this even — name it once.
